assumptions: the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: INV-R9’s gate read Object.keys(buckets) and treated every property it found as a valid disposition, so `exactly one bucket` meant `exactly one arbitrary JSON property`: GPT-5.6 moved a PROVED claim into an invented `dropped` bucket at exit 0, and separately moved one to the declared `rejected` bucket while the ledger still carried it as PROVED. Six claim dispositions and five file dispositions are now declared in scripts/integration-kernel.mjs with a contract each: `imported` binds provenance to the pinned material and refuses transferred authority; `already_present` needs a typed relation and an argument concluding it; `superseded` names an existing successor and refuses a candidate that also survives as live; `historical_only` names a revision scope; `rejected` refuses a candidate the ledger still carries as an import of this integration; `needs_adjudication` BLOCKS PROMOTION while non-empty. An undeclared bucket name is a refusal in either vocabulary.

coverage.domain: the declared claim and file disposition vocabularies
coverage.enumerator: the CLAIM_DISPOSITIONS and FILE_DISPOSITIONS tables, against which every bucket key is resolved

evidence_qualifiers.population: every bucket name in every integration manifest

attrs.gap: A CONTRACT IS A NECESSARY CONDITION, NOT A JUDGEMENT. `rejected` checks that a rejected candidate is not in the ledger as an import; it cannot check that rejecting it was right. `historical_only` checks a revision scope is named; it cannot check the claim is genuinely historical. The one disposition whose contract reaches its meaning is `already_present`, and only because the meaning was relocated into an argument — which is then DECLARED and not discharged (FAC-INTEGRATION-SUBSUMPTION). Second: four of the six dispositions are exercised by zero records in the only integration this tree has, so their contracts are checked by mutation controls rather than by production data. AND ONE CONTRACT TOOK TWO REFUSALS TO GET RIGHT, which is worth recording because both were the same mistake. The file-disposition contract first asked `does this path exist` — and README.md and two captured gate outputs are `build_product_not_content`, ABSENT from the source tree and PRESENT in the extraction, because the extraction is what the build writes them into. Asking the filesystem answered a question about a directory; the disposition is about the canonical set. The second attempt used three states — canonical, narrative, neither — and was refused too, because README.md is declared narrative with commit:false, which is a fact about how THIS lane ships it and not about what the source lane’s delta said it was. What a file disposition can mechanically carry is ONE BIT: is this path canonical source here. The finer distinction is prose in `means`.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9 audit §5, which asked for the closed vocabulary and named three of the mutations by hand.
attrs.review_focus: Four of six dispositions have no production record. Is a contract exercised only by its own mutation control evidence of anything beyond the control?
attrs.statement: The vocabulary of integration dispositions is CLOSED, and each disposition carries a contract on the target lane that the gate checks. Partitioning candidates into named buckets accounts for them only if the names mean something and the meaning is enforced.
